fullPassage: Some researchers view spoken languages as incomplete devices for capturing precise differences. They think numbers represent the most neutral language of description. However, when our language of description is changed to numbers, we do not move toward greater accuracy. Numbers are no more appropriate 'pictures of the world' than words, music, or painting. While useful for specific purposes (e.g. census taking, income distribution), they include information of enormous value. For example, the future lives of young students are tied to their scores on national tests. In effect, whether they can continue with their education, where, and at what cost depends importantly on a handful of numbers. These numbers do not account for the quality of schools they have attended, whether they have been tutored, have supportive parents, have test anxiety, and so on. Finally, putting aside the many ways in which statistical results can be manipulated, there are ways in which turning people's lives into numbers is morally insulating. Statistics on crime, homelessness, or the spread of a disease say nothing of people's suffering. We read the statistics as reports on events at a distance, thus allowing us to escape without being disturbed. Statistics are human beings with the tears wiped off. Quantify with caution.

questions.stem: 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 국가 시험이 학생의 미래에 미치는 긍정적 영향

det.korean: 이 글은 숫자를 통한 묘사의 한계와 문제점을 다루고 있다.
det.analysis:

det.tip: 글의 핵심: 숫자/통계는 인간의 질적 측면을 반영하지 못한다.

questions.passage: Some researchers view spoken languages as incomplete devices for capturing precise differences. They think numbers represent the most neutral language of description. questions.stem: 윗글의 요약문으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 숫자는 가장 객관적이고 정확한 묘사 도구이므로 적극 활용해야 한다.

det.korean: 숫자로의 전환은 정확성을 높이지 않으며, 인간적 고통을 외면하게 할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 글의 주장과 정반대

✅ ③ 글의 두 가지 핵심 주장을 정확히 요약

det.tip: 요약: 1) 숫자 ≠ 정확성 증가, 2) 통계 = 도덕적 차단(morally insulating)

questions.passage: Some researchers view spoken languages as incomplete devices for capturing precise differences. They think numbers represent the most neutral language of description. However, when our language of description is changed to numbers, we do not move toward greater accuracy. Numbers are no more appropriate 'pictures of the world' than words, music, or painting. While useful for specific purposes (e.g. census taking, income distribution), they include information of enormous value. For example, the future lives of young students are tied to their scores on national tests. In effect, whether they can continue with their education, where, and at what cost depends importantly on a handful of numbers. These numbers do not account for the quality of schools they have attended, whether they have been tutored, have supportive parents, have test anxiety, and so on. Finally, putting aside the many ways in which statistical results can be manipulated, there are ways in which turning people's lives into numbers is morally insulating. Statistics on crime, homelessness, or the spread of a disease say nothing of people's suffering. We read the statistics as reports on events at a distance, thus allowing us to escape without being disturbed. Statistics are ____ with the tears wiped off. Quantify with caution.

"통계는 눈물이 닦인 인간이다."

det.korean: 통계는 눈물이 닦인 인간(human beings)이다.
det.analysis: Statistics are human beings with the tears wiped off. — 원문 핵심 문장
det.tip: human beings = 인간. 통계의 비인간성을 역설적으로 표현한 문장.
